title: REVIEW
body:
Absolutely amazing! I’ve tried so many calendar/to-do apps, but none of them worked with my ADHD-brain except TickTick. Calendars, tasks, Eisenhower matrix, habit tracker, lists, event countdowns, notes, templates, summaries, Pomodoro timer and focus, and soooo much more - all of it in just one app. It also has such a beautiful and customizable design. And the app is available on all kinds of platforms. And to top it all off, you get a wonderful customer service too. I mean, it’s just incredible!

It’s abundantly clear to see how much work, thought and care you guys have put into this. Thank you so much for all your hard work! You guys are incredible!

title: Perfect combination of features
body: I am not new to this — over the years, I tried to build an optimal GTD-style productivity system in: Evernote, Things, OmniFocus and Todoist (not to mention countless attempts at custom solutions). I always ended up missing some elements I needed. E.g. with Todoist — the calendar view was underbaked, and I had to use Session for focus and time tracking. With the heavy-weight OmniFocus, with all customization options, the note support was abysmal. I have never felt more at home then I do with this app. It complements GTD in delightful ways: having trouble doing your weekly reviews or cleaning your inbox? Use the habit tracker! Some really big deadlines looming, but mixing with less important ones? Use Countdown. There’s more — The Pomodoro implementation  beats Session single - handedly in seamless integration with your task manager, while Session itself is almost twice the monthly price? The calendar is flexible, integrates without missing a beat, and is actually useful. Notes are fully realized, and can be used as a major part of the workflow. The API is quite flexible, if you want to ” roll your own” based on TickTick. The app works great on Mac, iPad, and iPhone. My only wish is custom dark themes — it was unexpected that customization applies to light themes only. The 1 dark theme is quite good though. Importantly, the app seems to click quite well with my ADHD too. Overall, cancelled my monthly subscriptions and went to annual within a week.

title: Amazing app, but lacking in some areas
body:
I have used TickTick for about a year now. It is absolutely one of the best ToDo-apps I have used (and I have used a lot!). 
But it’s lacking in three areas: 

1. Gamification. It has some badges but they are not very motivating and not very visible or integrated. I would really like more levels, and more “rewards” for the levels (maybe a new theme unlocking for example? I would also like to have different tasks weighted differently. If there is a task I have procrastinated for month, I would like to gather more points for completing it. 

2. “Nudging” feautures. I wish TickTick would take inspiration from Amazing Marvin which is superb in this area. They have feautures such as “task jar”, “random task”, “beat the clock”, “super focus mode”, “procrastination wizard” etc. 

3. Personalisation. Even though TickTick is already better in this area than many other apps in the same category, there is still A LOT of room for improvement. Again, I wish TickTick would learn from Amazing Marvin here. 

If these three areas were optimised, I would give TickTick a solid 10 out of 5!
